workItems.objective: Business no-show settlement integrity (handoff slice): processBusinessNoShow becomes ONE authoritative settlement transaction — canonical _refundEscrowTx refund -> guarded business-stake penalty claim -> conditional/idempotent booking terminal transition -> canonical AuditLog row -> COMMIT; plus guarded bookingEscrowService bucket drains.
workItems.notes: PR #244 (squash 66b39b1 on main), built on regression commit a1cacaf. Closes a live-main defect where the business no-show path was broken end-to-end: _refundEscrow was called with a human-readable reason string as the escrow lifecycle status (guaranteed enum violation); the stake penalty debited BusinessProfile.stakeBalance — a column that did not exist in the schema (penalties ALWAYS failed, swallowed); audit used entity/entityId/userId fields that do not exist (ALWAYS failed, swallowed). Fixes: escrowService exports its transaction-scoped financial primitives (incl. alias refundEscrowInTransaction) so other services reuse the canonical engine; penaltyPolicyService runs the whole settlement in one $transaction with NO swallowed failures (insufficient stake is a committed deterministic outcome penaltyApplied=false; unexpected DB errors roll back refund+stake+booking+audit together; replay against REFUNDED converges via alreadyProcessed with zero mutation and no duplicate audit rows); caller-supplied bookingId/businessProfileId verified against the escrow-linked booking before any mutation (BOOKING_ESCROW_MISMATCH/BUSINESS_MISMATCH); booking terminal transition uses real enum semantics — ReservationStatus.CANCELLED_BUSINESS / TransitBookingStatus.CANCELLED with pre-terminal guards (BOOKING_NOT_TRANSITIONABLE rolls back the settlement); bookingEscrowService release/refund/split-release payer-bucket drains are guarded conditional updateMany claims (ESCROW_BALANCE_INSUFFICIENT) instead of blind decrements; schema + additive migration 20260914120000_business_stake_balance add BusinessProfile.stakeBalance DECIMAL(20,8) DEFAULT 0 (safe on populated prod; note CI db push provisions it from schema.prisma). Tests: penalty-policy-integrity (7 mock-layer contract + 10 real-PostgreSQL cases: full settlement, exact-once penalty, insufficient stake, concurrent double no-show converges to one refund, concurrent penalty cannot take stake below zero, financial-failure full rollback, booking-transition full rollback, canonical audit persistence, replay zero-mutation, cross-booking/cross-business rejection) and penalty-policy-outcome rewritten to the guarded-claim architecture. First CI run failed on two test-authoring bugs only (required TransitBooking.bookingRef; error code lived only on err.code) — settlement logic was already correct (8/10 DB cases green) — fixed and CI green at exact head 8c6e24e (1181 tests); post-merge main-head run green at 66b39b1. Scope untouched: P2P trade settlement, withdrawals, SAT, admin RBAC, invoices, unrelated Business OS modules.

workItems.objective: Shift scheduling/state integrity (P0 handoff slice): createShift conflict-check+insert, updateShift time-change overlap check, and deleteShift stale-read-vs-clockIn all become race-proof — ONE serialized transaction per mutation under a transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock scoped to the employee schedule namespace, and a guarded conditional DELETE that is the authority against clockIn; no new state machine, no schema change, clockIn/clockOut/markNoShow lifecycle authority untouched.
workItems.notes: PR #247 (squash a6b025a on main). createShift: conflict check + insert in ONE transaction serialized by pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('business_shift_schedule:<employeeId>')) (acquired via tx, held until commit); businessProfileId added to the conflict predicate; tenant/inactive-employee checks and response shape preserved. updateShift: target loaded inside the transaction by id+businessProfileId; when startTime/endTime change, other active/scheduled shifts of the same employee/business (excluding the target) are checked under the SAME lock, rejecting overlap with the existing error; non-time updates skip overlap work entirely; caller-supplied status still rejected. deleteShift: guarded deleteMany (id+businessProfileId+status NOT CLOCKED_IN/LATE) inside a transaction; count!=1 re-reads and throws the exact existing errors; the conditional DELETE is the authority against clockIn (clockIn does not participate in the lock namespace) — clockIn untouched and not weakened. CRITICAL PLATFORM FINDING (CI-proven twice): pg_advisory_xact_lock() returns a void column that Prisma's query engine CANNOT deserialize in either $queryRaw form — both existing codebase patterns (tagged-template in orderTrackingMutationSafeService + storefrontDraft/PublishSafeService, $queryRawUnsafe in businessTaxPresetService) are latent CI failures that only pass because their tests never execute the lock path against real PostgreSQL. The working shape is 'SELECT 1 AS locked FROM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1))' via $queryRawUnsafe. FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED: apply the same one-line fix to businessTaxPresetService, orderTrackingMutationSafeService, and storefrontDraft/PublishSafeService, and add a DB-gated test that exercises each lock path. Tests: shift-scheduling-integrity (7 real-PostgreSQL cases: concurrent overlapping createShift exactly-one-winner, concurrent non-overlapping both succeed, concurrent time-changing updateShift cannot commit an overlapping schedule, update-to-overlap rejected zero-mutation, delete-vs-clockIn race ends consistent never a deleted active shift, business isolation, generic status mutation still rejected); shiftService.business-scope.test.js updated for the transactional updateShift call shape. Two intermediate CI failures were the void-deserialize discovery, then two test-design fixes (update-vs-update race redesigned so each update is valid alone but the results conflict; delete-race loosened to accept clockIn's guarded 'Shift was already resolved or clocked in.' when its pre-read beat the committed delete — invariants unchanged). CI green at exact head 9f6c466 (1212/1212 tests, route-check PASS, recovery drill clean); merged squash a6b025a. Scope untouched: marketplace, escrow/P2P, control plane, unrelated Business OS modules.

workItems.objective: Close the PR #240-flagged authority gap: APPROVAL_TIERS declares COMPLIANCE_ADMIN an eligible approver for the >= $10k tiers and the >= $50k invariant requires Finance-or-Compliance participation, but approveRequest()'s action-permission gate 403'd Compliance (catalog held no withdrawals.approve) before the tier logic could ever run — the tier declaration and the $50k invariant were dead letter for Compliance.
workItems.notes: PR #249 (merge commit dc701bb on main). Resolution chosen after tracing approveRequest/rejectRequest/createApprovalRequest, ADMIN_ROLES, APPROVAL_ACTION_PERMISSIONS, APPROVAL_TIERS, the tier/role eligibility helpers, the >= $50k invariant, the admin-rbac-approvals suite, the Admin Portal consumers (portal uses the direct withdrawal endpoints; the approval-request workflow is backend-API-only today), the CONTROL_PLANE_MANAGEMENT permission vocabulary, and PR #240's flagged tension. DECISION: catalog extension (one line), not tier-aware authorization — the tier system (isApprovalRoleEligible on the stored-amount tier + requiredApprovals + the >= $50k participation invariant) is already the sole amount-scoping authority; making the action permission amount-conditional would duplicate tier policy inside the permission gate (a second authorization dimension) and re-encode thresholds that APPROVAL_TIERS.requiredRoles already owns. Reuses the existing withdrawals.approve vocabulary (FINANCE_ADMIN entry) — no duplicate vocabulary. Resulting executable policy = declared policy: <$1k auto-approve; $1k-$10k any role holding withdrawals.approve (SUPER/FINANCE/COMPLIANCE/legacy ADMIN); $10k-$50k tier gate admits SUPER/FINANCE/COMPLIANCE (+legacy); >= $50k three approvals incl. the F/C invariant, now genuinely satisfiable by Compliance. Create/approve/reject all use the stored request type via the same action permission, so Compliance's create and rejection authority align automatically. Invariants preserved: SUPER_ADMIN/legacy ADMIN full authority, Finance unchanged, READ_ONLY gains nothing, self-approval forbidden, CAS writes untouched, no raw Prisma conflicts leak, no settlement/payout/socket/frontend changes, routes file untouched. Tests: 5 new mocked regressions (Compliance create / $10k-$50k approve end-to-end / Compliance OPENs the >= $50k chain completed by SUPER_ADMINs / reject alignment / approver identity asserted) + 1 new real-PostgreSQL proof (Compliance + Finance approve a $60k withdrawal CONCURRENTLY under the JSON-equality CAS, both interleaving outcomes handled, SUPER_ADMIN completes the 3-approval chain); stale NOTE in the $50k test replaced by the now-provable Compliance path. Verification: focused suite 34/34 on live Postgres 16 incl. 4 real-DB CAS proofs; route-check PASS; prisma validate clean; production audit 0 vulnerabilities; recovery drill SUCCESS; full suite 194/199 (same 5 pre-existing localhost:5432 failures as clean main 6be5399). Exact-head CI run #951 green at f2c836c; post-merge main-head run #952 at dc701bb.

workItems.objective: Make the AZM fee-discount debit atomic with the fiat withdrawal reservation so a failed reservation or provider reversal can never leave a consumed AZM spend with no withdrawal.
workItems.notes: PR #250 (squash 13d7884 on main). Pre-fix: applyFeeDiscount() committed the AZM debit in its own transaction BEFORE processFiatWithdrawal() ran, so a failed withdrawal reservation (fiat pool insufficient, balance check, DB error) or a later provider reversal left a consumed AZM spend with no withdrawal. Fix (additive, scoped to the fee-discount flow): azmSpendService exposes _debitAzmWithClient / applyFeeDiscountInTransaction(tx) debiting AZM on the canonical withdrawal transaction with deterministic dedup key fee_discount_<ref>; reverseFiatWithdrawal restores the exact spend once inside the reversal tx (PENDING->FAILED one-winner claim + metadata.reversedAt); controller emits azm_spend exactly once post-commit via emitFeeDiscountSpend(); AZM_SPEND_FAILED 400 contract preserved. New real-Postgres suite withdrawal-fee-discount-atomicity.test.js proves A-F incl. concurrent-reversal one-winner. Exact-head CI green at 8b1ac9c (200 suites / 1236 tests, CI-fresh ordering). Merged by Sugru 2026-09-15.

workItems.objective: Close two P0 integrity defects: force-cancel audit atomicity (War Room) and MTN payout unknown-outcome classification.
workItems.notes: PR #253 (squash 977f116 on main), branch verified against main f0f2f1c, no overlapping open PRs (issue #252). (1) Force-cancel audit atomicity: the DISPUTED->CANCELLED claim, escrow refund and ADMIN_INTERVENTION message committed in one tx, but the mandatory FORCE_CANCEL_TRADE audit row was written after the response through the fire-and-forget audit() helper which swallows failures — a committed financial cancellation could exist with zero audit evidence. audit() gained opt-in strict mode ({ throwOnError: true }); the trade claim, escrow refund, message AND audit row now commit in one transaction; concurrent cancels resolve deterministically (409 loser). (2) Payout unknown-outcome classification: MTN payout outcome classification so unknown-outcome withdrawals stay PROCESSING with a reconciliation exception instead of manual review; settle and replay idempotency. Two CI failure causes fixed en route: idempotent TEXT-key installer for the raw-SQL reconciliation tables (reference migrations had UUID keys that could never apply against TEXT transaction ids), and the force-cancel test now seeds its own admin instead of relying on a phantom user row from other suites. Full local validation: 203 suites / 1260 tests green on real PostgreSQL, CI-fresh ordering. Exact-head CI green. Merged by Sugru 2026-09-15.

workItems.objective: Close the P0 idempotency defect: concurrent identical AZM creditAzm()/debitAzm() calls could both mutate User.azmBalance because dedup was a read-then-write JSON-metadata pre-check with no database-level uniqueness.
workItems.notes: PR #254 (branch head 4fe4597 verified against main 977f116, squash 4efd269). Design: dedicated nullable dedupKey column + @@unique([userId, source, dedupKey]) on AzmRewardLog and AzmSpendLog — the DB unique index is the actual concurrency gate; a racing duplicate log insert fails the index and the WHOLE enclosing transaction (balance mutation included) rolls back. Additive history-preserving migration 20260915120000_azm_ledger_dedup_unique with a duplicate-audit NOTICE and first-occurrence-wins backfill (no ledger row deleted or rewritten); proven on real PostgreSQL incl. idempotent re-runs and a template-copy backup/restore drill. Services keep the fast-path pre-check, mirror dedupKey into metadata for compatibility, and converge P2002 races to the existing idempotent result semantics with winner-only post-commit socket emissions. azm-idempotency-concurrency suite: 8 real-PostgreSQL Promise.all() cases (concurrent credit/debit, replays, cross-user/cross-key independence, post-mutation rollback with retry) — regression-proven by reverting only the two service files (tests 1–2 fail with the double-credit/double-debit). Full battery 204/204 suites, 1268/1268 tests; route-check, prisma validate, production audit green. Exact-head CI green at 4fe4597; post-merge main-head run 34991074561 green at 4efd269. Merged by Sugru 2026-09-15.

workItems.objective: Close the P0 auction settlement defect: settle() burned winners via independent debitAzm() calls with swallowed errors, then unconditionally marked bids WON, boosted ads and SETTLED the auction — a winner without funds still got the full burn-free boost and the ledger/auction state permanently disagreed.
workItems.notes: PR #255 (branch head cf3b01e verified against main 4efd269, squash 6802ab6). Policy research per contract: no doc/spec/test defines an insufficient-funds fallback at settlement, so the fail-closed default applies — rollback, keep the auction retryable/OPEN; the existing 5-minute azm-auction worker is the recovery mechanism; no marketplace economics redesigned. Design: ONE authoritative settlement transaction — atomic OPEN→SETTLING conditional claim (window-closed, race-proof; zero rows converge to the existing skipped result), authoritative top-N selection inside the transaction, winner debits through the transaction-scoped _debitAzmWithClient primitive with deterministic auction-win-${auctionId}-${vendorId} dedup keys (exactly-once enforced by PR #254's unique invariant), WON/boost/LOST/SETTLED all in the same transaction, totalAzmBurned from actual committed debits, notifications + auction:settled emission strictly post-commit. A committed SETTLING is impossible under this design; legacy stranded SETTLING rows from the pre-atomic code are recovered burn-free via the widened claim + dedup keys. azm-auction-settlement-integrity suite: 9 real-PostgreSQL cases (success atomicity, concurrent settle exactly-one-winner, insufficient-balance fail-closed + recovery, post-debit rollback + retry, SETTLED replay no-op, legacy SETTLING recovery without reburn, rank ordering, zero bidders, auction isolation) — regression-proven: 4 cases fail on the old implementation. Full battery 205/205 suites, 1277/1277 tests; route-check, prisma validate, production audit and template-copy backup/restore drill (settled-auction rows + dedup gate survive restore, duplicate insert → P2002) all green. Diff 387+/113- = 500 changed lines, 2 files. Exact-head CI run 34993404805 green at cf3b01e; post-merge main-head CI green at 6802ab6. Merged by Sugru 2026-09-15.

workItems.objective: Close the deposit-address authority gap: User.tatumPolygonAddress was a single mutable legacy column with no registry, no lifecycle, and no global uniqueness — deposits resolved owners via string matching against a mutable field. Introduce the canonical WalletAddress registry: (address, network) globally unique at the DB level, exactly one ACTIVE row per user+asset identity (partial unique index), RETIRED addresses never reassigned, resolveOwner reads the registry first with the deterministic legacy-mirror fallback, canonical deposit identity is native Polygon USDC (0x3c499c542cef5e3811e1192ce70d8cc03d5c3359) with bridged USDC.e explicitly rejected, allocation is race-convergent, and the legacy mirror stays synced (never removed) for zero-downtime rollout.
workItems.notes: PR #275 (branch p0/wallet-address-authority, exact head 4ce3de4, squash ea75f05). Mechanism: migration 20260917150000_wallet_address_authority + boot installer infra/install-wallet-address-overlay.js (idempotent: enum DO-block, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, FK/index DO-blocks with duplicate_object tolerance, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING backfill of legacy mirror addresses with derivationIndex = user.id); services/walletAddressService.js is the single allocation/retirement/query authority. Proofs: custody-execution suite grown 57→72 tests on real PostgreSQL (exact payload contract, validator accept/refuse matrix + route with IP allowlist, concurrent CAS single-winner, crash-ambiguous retry, settlement refusal without evidence incl. forged-proof attempt, registry fail-closed/mismatch, mainnet four-eye gating); zero regressions (the 11 failing full-suite suites are pre-existing localhost:5432 environment suites, identical on clean main); route-check PASS, prisma validate, production audit 0 vulnerabilities, db-recovery-drill SUCCESS. workItems.notes: §P.5-B completed and verified. PR #281 final head fb56d06, squash-merged to backend main as 39a4977. InventoryLot is immutable-on-acquire (unique acquisitionKey; replay returns committed lot; conflicting reuse fails closed INVENTORY_ACQUISITION_CONFLICT); quantityOriginal/costBasisGhs exact via ledger.toExactDecimal; remaining derived from original minus consumed movements with DB CHECK 0<=remaining<=original (CI db push path has no raw CHECKs; enforcement rests on the atomic updateMany claim). Acquisition posts single-asset USDC through ledgerService.post() (INVENTORY_ACQUISITION, inventory:usdc:lots debit / equity:treasury credit). Concurrency: updateMany({status OPEN, remaining>=q}) atomic claim; loser fails closed and enclosing transaction rolls back. Consumption replay/conflict closed under unique consumptionKey.
